summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for aspirin desensitization to enable further cardiac evaluation after a prior NSTEMI. She had a history of aspirin allergy with hives and shortness of breath, requiring inpatient desensitization. Her renal function was impaired (creatinine 1.9) due to prior contrast-induced nephropathy and hypertensive injury, delaying cardiac catheterization. Prehydration and Mucomyst were given for renal protection. Aspirin desensitization was completed successfully without reaction. Cardiac catheterization revealed stable two-vessel coronary disease not amenable to stenting, and cardiothoracic surgery is evaluating her for bypass pending optimization of comorbidities. Blood pressure was controlled with hydralazine and amlodipine; labetolol was restarted post-desensitization. Lisinopril and lasix were held due to renal concerns. She was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with strict instructions to continue daily aspirin to avoid repeat desensitization, monitor weight, and follow up with cardiology and primary care.
